sections.content: How many people stayed in Lymington after gaining qualifications?

Lymington is a small town in the South East. Lymington does not have its own university.

Lymington has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Lymington ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 560 state-school pupils from Lymington who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 155 (28%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 190 (34%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Lymington to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Lymington's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Lymington in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Lymington move to?

Of Lymington's graduates, 80 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Lymington's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 70 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those qualified non-graduates (36%) were living fairly locally, in the Southampton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Lymington's GCSE cohort:

  • 55 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 35 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East

In 2018 to 2019, 33% of graduates and 28% of qualified non-graduates living in Lymington had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 105 graduates and 160 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Lymington. This is compared with the 155 graduates and 190 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 67% of the graduates had also lived in Lymington as GCSE pupils, while 33% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Lymington in 2018 to 2019, 72% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 28% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
